summary.one_liner: A DevSecOps reference project that runs a multi-arch Flask API and the intentionally vulnerable OWASP Juice Shop through a GitHub Actions security pipeline, with image signing, Kyverno admission policies, and ArgoCD GitOps deployment to AWS and a Raspberry Pi k3s cluster.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds a Flask API, a hardened Juice Shop Dockerfile, Terraform for AWS (VPC, ALB, EC2, ECR, IAM), and Kustomize/ArgoCD manifests for a Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster. The GitHub Actions pipeline runs Bandit SAST, Trivy secret and container scans, Syft/CycloneDX SBOM generation, Cosign image signing by digest, Checkov IaC scanning, and OWASP ZAP baseline and full scans. After a build, the pipeline commits @sha256 digests into overlay patch-image.yaml files, and ArgoCD syncs them to the cluster. Kyverno ClusterPolicies verify signatures and enforce non-root, no privileged containers, read-only root filesystems, and resource limits at admission. Public ingress to the Pi goes through an in-cluster cloudflared Deployment, so the Pi has no open inbound ports. The README also includes a troubleshooting ledger of fourteen issues and their fixes.
use_cases: learn a DevSecOps CI/CD pipeline end to end
run Trivy, Bandit, ZAP and Checkov scans in GitHub Actions
sign container images with Cosign and enforce with Kyverno
GitOps deployment to a k3s cluster with ArgoCD
expose a homelab service through Cloudflare Tunnel without open ports
demonstrate admission control blocking a root container
how_to_run: docker build -t devsecops-api . && docker run -p 5000:5000 devsecops-api
cd terraform/aws && terraform init && terraform apply -var="key_pair_name=devsecops-key" -var="allowed_ssh_cidr=<your-ip>/32"
notable: Kyverno admission policies block the official root-running Juice Shop image and admit only the pipeline-hardened, signed build
Deploys are Git commits: the pipeline writes image digests to patch-image.yaml and ArgoCD syncs them, so rollback is git revert
Security gates are a mix of hard-fail (secret scan, Flask CRITICAL CVEs, unsigned images) and report-only (Juice Shop scans)
Troubleshooting ledger documents fourteen real build issues such as multi-arch exec format errors, Kyverno digest lookups, and Cloudflare ingress ordering
Includes a known-gaps table listing accepted risks such as missing NetworkPolicies and no runtime security
caveats: AWS cloud environment is described as on-demand and often destroyed to avoid cost
Requires many external accounts and secrets, including AWS OIDC role, Cosign keys, a GitHub App, and Slack webhook
Live Pi endpoints and ECR paths are specific to the author's setup and are not generic deployment targets
